entries.title: !intro
entries.summary: Pepe introduces himself to the whole room: who he is, what PAT is, and where to start.
entries.details: Two short lines in the room: Pepe is the room's frog bot (games, heists, music, voice, the PublicAccess economy), PAT is the room's coin you earn by hanging out, chatting and playing, and `!balance`, `!spin` and `!help` are good first commands. Anyone can use it; once per room every 10 minutes (inside that, Pepe answers you by PM instead).

entries.title: !language [code|auto]
entries.summary: Which language Pepe speaks in this room - he follows the room's chat on his own, or a mod fixes it.
entries.details:
`!language` shows this room's setting and the language Pepe has detected (with how much of the recent chat it makes up). By default it's **auto**: Pepe watches the room's recent chat and mic and answers in whatever language clearly dominates - a few lines in another language never flip it, it switches only after a language holds most of the chat from at least two people for a couple of minutes. His AI replies and the most common command lines (balance, spin, tips, heists, raffle, `!help`, `!intro`) come out in that language; usernames and commands stay as they are.

**Room mods fix it** with `!language <code>` (`es`, `pt`, `fr`, `de`, `it`, `nl`, `pl`, `tr`, `ru`, `uk`, `ar`, `fa`, `hi`, `id`, `vi`, `th`, `ja`, `ko`, `zh`, `zh-tw`, or the name, like `!language spanish`) and go back with `!language auto`. Mods = Pepe admins, the room's owner and its red list (the same people as `!snap on`).

entries.title: !time [place|user] · !time set [zone]
entries.summary: Free.
entries.details: Free. `!time` shows the time in ET, PT and the UK; `!time tokyo` (or any city or zone) shows it there; `!time <user>` shows theirs if they've set it. `!time set chicago` saves your own zone — then `!remind me at 9pm` means your 9pm. `!time unset` goes back to ET.

entries.title: PM Pepe
entries.summary: Message Pepe privately and he answers privately.
entries.details:
Message Pepe privately and he answers privately. He has the **same context he'd have in the room** — who's there, what's been said and micced recently, what's playing, who's on cam — so "what's X on about?" works in a DM.

**He remembers your DMs, privately.** Anything you tell him in a PM is tagged to you and only ever surfaces when he's talking to you in a PM. It never goes into public chat, never becomes room lore, never shows up in anyone else's context, and isn't searchable.

The gate is **who told him**, not who it's about. Tell him your opinion of someone in a DM and he'll remember it for you next time you two talk — and he'll say none of it to them. He won't repeat what anyone else has told him privately either; ask and he'll tell you that straight.

It works one way: a **PM includes everything he knows publicly** — the room, what's been said and micced, who's around — plus what you've told him privately. Public chat gets only the public half.

entries.title: !incognito · !forgetme on|off
entries.summary: Your own switch: with incognito on, nothing you say gets remembered at all — in the room or in PMs — and you show as "someone" on the website. Also on the website: Settings → Privacy.
entries.details:
Your own switch: with incognito **on**, nothing you say gets remembered at all — in the room or in PMs — and anything still waiting to be processed is binned. **Off by default.** It stops new memories — it doesn't erase what he already knows (ask an admin if you want that wiped). Works from a PM or the room, and the reply always comes back privately.

While it's on you're also private on the website: "someone" on the live room view (your lines aren't shown), captures of you are private, nobody can quote you or use your cam in AI pictures, and your top words aren't recorded in your profile analytics.

The same switch is on the website at [/settings/privacy](/settings/privacy) (Settings → Privacy) for a linked chat account - a change in either place shows in the other.

entries.title: Telegram
entries.summary: Pepe on Telegram: your alerts, and with a Season Pass his commands and a chat with him.
entries.details:
Link Telegram at publicaccess.tv → Settings → Telegram (or Edit profile → Connections): you get a one-time code, open Pepe's bot and press Start. Linking is free and brings your alerts to Telegram - direct messages, room mentions, tips, follows / go-live and any other notice kind you switch on.

A Telegram spend has no room, so it goes to Fort Knox. Casino games, wagers, markets, loans, heists, moderation and anything that needs Pepe in a room aren't available. Anything that isn't a command is a chat with Pepe, priced like Message Pepe.

entries.title: !quote last N | @user N | from <words> to <words>
entries.summary: Turn a bit of the room's chat into a quote post on its pad (bash.org style) - 250 PAT, 40% to the people quoted.
entries.details:
Pepe turns the room's recent lines - chat and 🎙 mic transcripts - into a **quote post** on the room's pad and posts the link. `!quote last 5` takes the last 5 lines (commands left out), `!quote @user 3` that person's last 3 lines with the lines around them, `!quote from <words> to <words>` everything from the line with the first words to the line with the second. Add `| a title` at the end for a title. Up to 20 lines.

A quote costs **250 PAT** from your linked PATV account (admins free); **40%** of it goes to the people quoted (a likeness royalty, paid after a 24 h hold), and anyone who typed `!likeness clips off` can't be quoted.

Only lines the website already shows can be quoted - never private messages, and people who are `!incognito` or typed `!bridge hide` show as "someone". Anyone quoted can tap **Remove me** on the website to show their lines as "someone". The room must be bridged to its pad (`!bridge on`). Free, a few per half hour. A pad's best quotes: publicaccess.tv/p/<pad>/quotes (with the Quote of the day).

entries.title: !bridge [hide|show]
entries.summary: Is this room live on its PATV pad?
entries.details: Is this room live on its PATV pad? Bridged rooms (Pepe's Pad by default) show their public chat, who's here, who's on the mic and the topic, read-only, to signed-in users on their pad at `publicaccess.tv/p/<name>` (all pads: `publicaccess.tv/p`). PMs never go there. `!bridge hide` makes you "someone" on the website (no name, your lines not shown); `!incognito on` does the same. Mic transcripts show in the feed too. Admins: `!bridge on|off`, `!bridge transcripts on|off`, and `!bridge audio on|off` (off by default: streams the room's audio live to signed-in members, nothing recorded; Pepe announces it in the room). With net audio each room with audio on streams its own sound; without it only the `!audioroom` room can, and `!bridge` says why a room's audio isn't streaming. Messages typed on the pad reach the room in about a second (paced so the room isn't flooded); `!bridge fast off` (admins) falls back to the slower sync-only relay.

entries.title: !livecam [off|on]
entries.summary: Can people on the website see your cam (live, snapshots, clips)?
entries.details: Signed-in members of a room's PATV pad can see someone's cam on the website: press **▶ Live** to watch it live (Pepe relays it, about a second behind; nothing is recorded), take a snapshot or record a short clip. Everyone is in by default: `!livecam off` keeps your cam off the website completely - no live video, snapshots or clips, and any live relay stops at once; `!livecam on` allows it again. It's the same switch as Settings → Privacy on publicaccess.tv. `!bridge hide` and `!incognito on` keep your cam off the website too. Whenever someone opens your cam there, Pepe tells you by PM who it was (`!whowatching` shows everyone; `!blockviewer <name>` blocks one person). `!livecam` shows your setting. Admins: `!bridge livecams on|off` per room (needs `!bridge cams on`).

entries.title: !onair me on|off
entries.summary: May admins put your cam on Pepe's main stream?
entries.details: Admins can put a live pad stream or someone's Camfrog cam on Pepe's main stream for a while - it then shows on publicaccess.tv, on Pepe's Twitch relay and on Pepe's own cam here. A cam needs its owner's OK first: `!onair me on` allows it, `!onair me off` says no (the same switch as Settings → Privacy on publicaccess.tv; `!livecam off`, `!bridge hide` and `!incognito on` always keep your cam off it). Pepe tells you when your cam goes on, and `!onair off` takes your own cam or stream off at once. `!onair` shows what's on. Admins: `!onair <pad|user|slot id>` puts a live slot on, `!onair cam <login>` someone on cam in this room, `!onair off` ends it, `!onair setup` adds the media source to Pepe's OBS once; `!onair setup irl` keeps the IRL feed's receiver open while hidden so OBS can switch to it when it goes live from BRB / Gaming (`!onair setup irl-off` undoes it). YouTube / Twitch embed slots need `rights` at the end (`!onair <pad|user> rights`) to confirm you may rebroadcast them; `!onair setup embed` adds their browser source once. A slot on an Approved-only pad or a cam without an opt-in waits for its owner's OK: the owner gets an instant request, and a cam owner answers Pepe's PM with `!onair yes` (this time), `!onair always` or `!onair no`. entries.title: !whowatching

entries.details: Pepe PMs you who has your cam open: on the website (watching it **live** right now, plus anyone who took a snapshot or a clip in the last 30 minutes, with their PATV and Camfrog names) and in Camfrog itself (Pepe asks the server with `/whowatching` - the server only answers him where he has room powers; your own Camfrog always shows who's viewing you). Only about your own cam; admins can name anyone. The same list is in Settings → Privacy on publicaccess.tv. Block someone from the website with `!blockviewer <name>`.

entries.details: `!blockviewer <name>` stops that PATV account from opening your cam on the website - no live view, no snapshots, no clips; if they're watching live right now it ends at once, and they're only told your cam isn't available. `<name>` is their PATV name or their Camfrog name (Pepe's PM about who opened your cam tells you which to type). `!unblockviewer <name>` lets them back, `!blockviewer` on its own lists who you blocked. It's the same list as Settings → Privacy on publicaccess.tv. It's about the website only - inside Camfrog, use Camfrog's own ignore. To keep your cam off the website for everyone: `!livecam off`.

entries.title: !ghost [on|off]
entries.summary: 👻 Ghost mode for site staff: open cams on the website without telling the owner - always audited.
entries.details: For moderation. While it's on, opening someone's cam on the website (live, a snapshot or a clip) doesn't send them Pepe's PM, you aren't listed in their `!whowatching` or the privacy page's who's-watching list, you aren't counted in the viewer numbers, and Pepe leaves it out of the room's mod log. It's never silent: every ghost view and every switch on or off is logged for the admins (Admin → Pepe → Live cams). It doesn't get past anyone's choices - a cam switched off for the website (`!livecam off`), kept private or blocked to you stays closed. Only accounts whose PATV class is Admin or Staff can switch it on; the same switch is in Settings → Privacy. `!ghost` on its own shows your setting.

entries.title: !bridge block <name> [global] [duration] [reason]
entries.summary: Stop someone talking into this room from the website (the pad page's relay) - for a while or until lifted.
entries.details:
Blocks a website member's **web relay** into this room: their chat lines, voice clips, typed `!commands` and the Pepe menu from the pad page. It doesn't touch normal Camfrog chat - someone with a linked chat name still talks in the room as usual (that's what `!kick` / `!ban` / `!timeout` are for).

`<name>` is how the room sees them (`🌐name`), their PATV username, or their chat name. Durations: `30m`, `2h`, `1d`, `7d`, or `perm` (until lifted, the default); the rest of the line is the reason they're shown.

Who: this room's mods, the pad's owner and Pepe admins. `global` (Pepe admins only) blocks them in every room. `!bridge blocks` lists this room's blocks (and the global ones); `!bridge unblock <name>` lifts one.

The list lives on publicaccess.tv (the pad's owner page and /admin/bridge show and change it too); Pepe keeps a copy, so a block still holds if the website is down - but a new block or unblock needs the website to answer.

Tickets are **PAT 1,000** and there's no limit on how many you hold. The draw is **every Sunday at 9pm ET**, announced in every room and revealed ball by ball on the stream; sales close 5 minutes before. **The jackpot has its own pot**: 40% of every ticket goes into it and it rolls over until someone hits it (then the Federal Reserve restarts it at 1M); the other 60% goes to the casino (the House), which pays the fixed prizes. Capped at 100M. **Prizes:** all 4 + Pepe Ball = the **JACKPOT** (1 in 274,050, split between winners) · 4 = 500k · 3 + PB = 150k · 3 = 15k · 2 + PB = 7.5k · 1 + PB = 3k · Pepe Ball only = 1.5k · 2 = 1k. He then calls a number every few seconds in chat and on the overlay. **You have to call it yourself:** type `!bingo` the moment one of your cards has a complete line — a row, column or diagonal (the centre is free) — and Pepe checks it against the numbers called so far, so you don't need to mark anything. The first line wins **30%** of the prize pool; play continues and the first **full card** wins the rest. Two valid calls on the same ball split the prize. **A wrong call costs PAT 1,000** (it goes into the pot) and benches you for 60 seconds. `!bingo card` re-sends your cards with the called numbers crossed out (XX). 10% of card sales goes to the casino. If nobody calls a prize before all 75 balls are out, it **rolls over** into the next game. Needs at least 2 players; if Pepe restarts mid-game, every card is refunded.

entries.title: !reserve
entries.summary: The 🏛️ Federal Reserve — the central bank: the only place new PAT is made, and it only fills the protocol's pools.
entries.details: The **🏛️ Federal Reserve** — the central bank and the only place new PAT is made. Anyone can check the balance. It keeps itself between a **floor (50M)** and a **ceiling (150M)**: below the floor a capped daily mint tops it back up, above the ceiling the excess is burned. Every Monday it tops the incentive budget up to the week's target (25M), it lends the House, the Bank and the Market maker the gap when a payout runs them short (flash liquidity), and it collects fines, the bounty fee and the shop fee plus half of the protocol's weekly profit while it's below its ceiling. Every mint is logged and the supply history is public on [publicaccess.tv/economy](https://publicaccess.tv/economy). **Economy v2/v3** (layers on): the Fed is the protocol's backstop - nobody robs it, it pays no rewards and never pays a wallet (`!reserve pay` is off), and it mints only by written policy. `!reserve mint <amount> <reason>` is the admin mint into the Fed (the same as `!econ mint`). It fills the protocol's pools two ways, admins only, dry run + confirm, logged: a **grant** (`!reserve fund <pool> <amount> <reason>` = `!econ fund`, not repayable) or a **loan** (`!econ fedloan <pool> <amount> <reason>`, repaid from that pool's surplus or overflow). The old automint (`!reserve auto` / `!reserve floor`) is off while the layers are on; the v3 floor and ceiling replace it.

entries.title: !econ
entries.summary: The economy layers at a glance: the Federal Reserve (and its loans to the Treasury vaults), Fort Knox and the incentive budget.
entries.details: Shows each layer's balance and whether the economy v2 layers are on. Admins: `!econ layers on|off`, `!econ roomvaults on|off` (pad vaults, economy v2 E-3: room spending goes 50/50 to Fort Knox and the pad's vault; needs the layers on), `!econ recipe` (the room payout recipe: `cutover` [confirm <id>], `on|off`, `preview [room]`, `run`, `cfg`; `!econ vwm [status [YYYY-MM-DD]]|on|off` pays the streamer slice on verified watch-minutes (E-5); `!econ convoys on|off` puts payouts of 25k+ on hittable convoys (E-7); `!econ challenges on|off|cfg` holds mic-challenge prizes from the pad vault, with prize gates and open-round entry fees (E-8); pad top-ups: `!econ activitypads preview|on|off`, profile vaults: `!econ profilevaults on|off`), `!econ roomvaults migrate` (moves the pads' pad-vault escrow on the website into their pad vaults - a dry run first, then `!econ roomvaults confirm <id>`),`!econ fortknox migrate` (a dry run first, then `!econ fortknox confirm <id>`), `!econ seed` (the one-time opening balances: the Bank's idle protocol capital above its target tops Fort Knox up to 2M and the rest goes to the incentive budget - a dry run first, then `!econ seed confirm <id>`; nothing is minted), `!econ fedmint` (the one-time cutover mint that topped the Federal Reserve up to 25M, done 2026-10-09 - a dry run first, then `!econ fedmint confirm <id>`), `!econ fedloan` (lists the Federal Reserve's outstanding liquidity loans; `!econ fedloan <house|bank|mm> <amount> <reason>` previews a loan to a Treasury vault whose PAT is below its hard floor - House 5M, Bank 1M, Market maker 0.5M - and whose value is below its target, capped at the gap and at 10M outstanding in total, minting the shortfall under the loan policy if the Fed is short; then `!econ fedloan confirm <id>` within 2 minutes. Treasury loans are repaid first from that vault's weekly surplus. `!econ fedloan fortknox|casino <amount> <reason>` lends to Fort Knox or the Casino vault, up to the pool's cap and inside the same 10M; it is repaid first from that pool's overflow above its cap (the daily release pays the Fed before the incentive budget) or early with `!econ fedloan repay <id> [amount]` (dry run + confirm). The incentive budget, the lotto pot and pad vaults are grant only (`!econ fund`): they have no surplus of their own to repay from. The Bank's loan-default insurance opens one automatically when its own surplus can't cover a default), `!econ check`, `!econ get [key]` (the economy v2 floors, targets, caps and weekly budgets - every number on the admin panel's Federal Reserve & floors card - with their defaults; one key shows its value, default and label), `!econ set <key> <value>` (changes one, e.g. `!econ set fortknox_floor 2.5m`; `!econ set <key> default` puts it back; validated - whole PAT, floor at most the target / cap, weekly budgets at most 100M in total - applied at once and logged on the card; keys: house_target, house_hard_floor, bank_target, bank_hard_floor, bank_lent_mult_pct, bank_peak_days, mm_target, mm_hard_floor, fedloan_cap, fortknox_floor, fortknox_cap, casino_floor, casino_cap (above either cap the daily release sends the overflow into the incentive budget), budget_<group> and pace_<group> (days a group's week is spread over, 0 = not paced) for welcome, levelup, achievements, misc, royalties, roomgames, turf, season, launchpad), `!econ monetary` (economy v3: the Federal Reserve's band - it mints back up to its floor (default 25M, 50M on prod), at most 5M a day, and releases what is above its ceiling, 150M, to the burn or the incentive budget - the Monday incentive guarantee, organic issuance and Fed flash liquidity), `!econ mints` (this month's mints per source - issuance, floor, admin, loans, restores, donations, seed - against their monthly caps, and the latest mints), `!econ mint <amount> <reason>` (an admin mint into the Federal Reserve only - never a pool or a wallet; a dry run first, then `!econ mint confirm <id>`; logged, no cap of its own, counted in the monthly total cap), `!econ fund <house|bank|mm|fortknox|casino|incentives|lotto|room:<id>> <amount> <reason>` (a Fed grant: moves PAT the Fed holds into that pool, not repayable, nothing minted - a dry run first, then `!econ fund confirm <id>`; a grant that takes the Fed below its floor is flagged and needs the confirm twice - the next daily tick mints the Fed back up inside the caps; Fort Knox, the Casino vault and pad vaults take at most what fits under their cap; also the admin panel's "Fill a pool from the Reserve" form, grant or loan), `!econ fedseed <total> [reason]` (mints the Federal Reserve up to <total>, once per total - a dry run first, then `!econ fedseed confirm <id>`), `!econ flash` (the Fed's flash liquidity: when a player loan, a House payout or a market seed is bigger than the Bank, the House or the Market maker can pay, the Fed lends that vault the gap, inside the Fed loan cap; an admin action that draws on it asks for a second confirm), `!econ set` also takes the v3 keys: fed_floor, fed_ceiling, fed_floor_mint_daily, fed_ceiling_action burn|incentives, incentive_guarantee on|off, issuance_mode off|pct|fixed, issuance_pct_month, issuance_fixed_month, issuance_activity_scaling, mintcap_<issuance|floor|loan|restore|total> (a number or unlimited; the admin mint counts toward mintcap_total), flash_bank / flash_house / flash_mm on|off, grant_weekly_cap, donation_rate, donation_bonus_pct, staker_share_pct, fed_split_pct, room_vault_cap, `!econ launchpad` (the pad launchpad: new pads build momentum - regulars who keep coming back - toward launch grants from the incentive budget into their pad vault, plus newcomer welcomes, owner deposit matching and front-page boost credit; `!econ launchpad on|off`, `!econ launchpad set <key> <value>` for every number, `!econ launchpad tier <n> <regulars> <active days> <grant>`, `!econ launchpad pads|grants`; graduations are approved on the website's admin economy page). `!econ` also shows the Fed loans outstanding.

entries.details: Every pad has a **pad vault**, connected to a chat room or not. Paid commands, songs, voices, heist gear and other spending in a connected room go half to the pad's vault and half to Fort Knox (until room payouts start, the owner's 10% royalty comes first on commands in a pad with an owner). Boosts, stage-slot fees and pad cosmetic gifts on the website do the same. The pad owner, or the gang that controls the room, spending in their own room sends it all to Fort Knox, and a vault holds at most 50M (anything above goes to Fort Knox). `!padvault` shows the balance, the last 7 days' inflow and deposits; `!padvault deposit 5000` adds your own PAT (minimum 1,000; add `anon` to keep your name off the pad's public donation list; deposits never count as the pad's income); `!padvault history` lists the latest moves; `!padvault all` lists the biggest vaults. Once room payouts are on, every vault pays out once a day through the **payout recipe**: a budget of the owner's daily rate (2-15%, 10% by default, picked on the pad page) of its balance, split into owner 15% (when they were active 3 of the last 7 days and the pad was active 3 of them - either place counts: in the connected room, or on the pad itself (posting, commenting, streaming, moderating; days with 3+ qualified members active there); capped at 25% of the room's average daily income; house pads never pay an owner), the controlling gang 15%, streamers 25% (verified watch-minutes on the pad's stage), regulars 35% (10+ real chat lines or 5+ minutes of heard speech that day, a PATV account a week old; with activity top-ups on, also members whose posts on the pad got real engagement) and room games 10% (the day's prize pool for the raffle, top mic and pictionary; XP only once it's used). Each slice pays only what was earned; the rest stays in the vault. With convoys on, payouts of 25,000 or more ride a 10-minute convoy (`!hit`); otherwise every payout is paid at once. `!padvault recipe` shows the room's last payout day. entries.title: Where drops come from
entries.summary: Some gear can't be bought: it drops when you win something, and Pepe announces it in the room.
entries.details:
Some gear can't be bought: it **drops** when you win something, and Pepe announces it in the room. Rarer items drop less often. Chances per winner:

• **Vault cracked** (casino / bank heist): 25% for each robber. **Arena champion**: 10%. **Bingo**: full card 10%, line 5%. **Paid-out bounty** (10,000+ pot): 15% each hunter, 5% the creator, with bounty-only gear.

• **Everyday wins** (low on purpose, so a drop still means something): convoy taken 5% · duel or brawl won 3% (stake 10,000+) · vault door reached but it held 2% · lotto prize 2% (once per draw) · blackjack natural up to 2% (bet 2,500+; the full 2% at a 10,000+ bet) · hold'em showdown pot 1.5% (pot 20,000+) · clean store getaway 1% · **wheel spin 0.05%** (1 in 2,000).

• **Jackpots**: hitting the lotto jackpot always drops a rare-or-better item; the wheel's jackpot slice has a 25% chance of one.

• Everyday wins give at most **3 drops per 24 hours** per player. Duels and brawls only count against a real opponent (not yourself or your alt, both level 2+), and only the first 3 wins between the same two players each day can drop. Nothing drops until the win has actually been paid.

entries.details: Open a **prediction market** anyone can trade — `!market new Will Samira come back this week? judge @carol closes 2d`. Yes/no by default, or give 2–6 answers with `options red/blue/green`. Markets trade **shares**, like Polymarket: each answer has a price between 0 and 1 PAT (the crowd's odds), and every share of the winning answer pays **1 PAT**. Buy with `!market M3 yes 5k` (spend 5k PAT, min 500) — buying pushes the price up, selling pushes it down. Sell any time while trading is open with `!market sell M3 yes 300` or `all`, so you can lock in a profit (or cut a loss) before the result. `!market mine` shows your positions with your entry price, today's price and profit/loss; `!market M3` the prices, `!market list` the open ones. 2% fee on every buy and sell. Trading closes at the set time — a duration (`closes 2d`) or a date (`closes 2026-11-03 18:00 ET`, any zone name; default 1 day, within the admins' limits, normally 1 hour to 90 days) — and the AI judge is only asked after it; the judge — who can't trade — calls it with `!market settle M3 yes`, or `!market settle M3 void <reason>`. **On a void, trading fees are not refunded** (they were taken when you traded): the Federal Reserve takes back its seed first, then holders split what's left in the market, up to what they put in — so if others sold at a profit before the void, holders get back less. Betting pools and wagers are different: a void there refunds every stake in full, fees included. All of it, judging included, works on [publicaccess.tv/markets](https://publicaccess.tv/markets) with a price chart. The Federal Reserve seeds each market's liquidity and gets back whatever's left over. Start one from the site too. For the old simple pool model, see `!pool`.

entries.title: !gang withdraw · !gang limits
entries.summary: The treasury is a shared pot you draw from, not a payroll.
entries.details:
The treasury is a **shared pot you draw from**, not a payroll. There's no daily wage any more — income stays banked and each member takes what they need up to **their rank's daily allowance**: owner unlimited, officer 250,000, member 100,000, recruit 25,000. Allowances are **per person**, so one officer emptying theirs no longer locks out the rest of the crew, and they reset on the daily tick.

`!gang limits` shows the current allowances; the boss sets them with `!gang limits <owner|officer|member|recruit> <amount>` (0 = unlimited). Withdrawals pay a **5% laundering cut** to Fort Knox (the vault bank heists rob) on the way out.

entries.title: !gangs reset
entries.summary: The start-over button.
entries.details: The start-over button. Wipes **every** gang — members, treasuries, rep, Turf Score — and clears the whole map, banks and stakes included. Nothing is refunded and there's no undo, so it asks for `!gangs reset confirm`. Distinct from a season ending, which keeps rep and hands stakes back.

entries.title: !turf season · !claim
entries.summary: Turf Score is the season standing, separate from gang rep.
entries.details:
**Turf Score** is the season standing, separate from gang rep. It builds every day you hold a borough — outer 1, mid 2, centre 4 per day (×100) — so a season is won by holding ground over time, not by sweeping the map on the last day. Holding at the final whistle adds up to +25%. `!turf season` shows the table, the day, and the prize pot.

It's also the **invasion gate**: 500 to move on a mid borough, 2,000 for Mayfair. Earned this season, so an old gang doesn't start with the map unlocked.

**Claiming is a crew event.** `!claim <borough>` musters for 45s — crewmates `!join` for 5,000 PAT each — then the whole crew rolls against whoever's already there. 8 rounds outer, 9 mid, 10 centre, 2 strikes each, and numbers genuinely tell (a crew bonus applies from 3 up). Geared success runs about **24% solo · 68% at three · 89% at five** on an outer borough, **39%** at five for a mid one and **17%** for Mayfair — so the crown needs a real gang. **The stake is only paid if you take it**: a failed run costs the buy-ins, never the deposit.

**Season end** (30 days, or `!turf end`): the top score takes the pot — everything the streets banked, matched from the incentive budget. If nobody scored, the pot rolls over into next season's. Business banks go to the Federal Reserve, convoy cargo still on its way goes to Fort Knox, and **every stake is refunded** — holding turf is never a losing move (a disbanded gang's stake goes to its members). Ownership, banks and Turf Score reset; gang rep is permanent and carries over. London's season 4 is the **last borough season**: after it the war moves to the rooms themselves (`!room`).

entries.title: !heist convoy · !defend · !turf cargo
entries.summary: Every business queues its takings as cargo instead of banking them on the spot.
entries.details:
Every business queues its takings as **cargo** instead of banking them on the spot. Since 2026-10-11 the casino rake, the fight rake, songs, voices, shout-outs, `!say`, cosmetics and heist gear no longer feed the businesses: that share goes to the vault of the room the PAT was spent in, `!fortify` supplies go to Fort Knox and the wheel cut is gone (the House keeps all wheel turnover), so for the rest of the season businesses earn mostly from tips. Every so often an **armored convoy** leaves carrying the lot — announced in the room, naming the business and the haul — and for **15 minutes** it's on the road and takeable.

**Rivals only:** `!heist convoy` intercepts it. You can't rob your own gang's PAT. The prize is the cargo itself — every round's loot comes out of it, and survivors split whatever's left; no vault, no door — and the owners never see a penny of what's taken.

**Owners:** `!defend` to ride shotgun. Each guard raises every DC on that run, so a well-escorted convoy is a genuinely bad idea to hit.

If nobody takes it (or the crew gets pinched), what's left of the cargo banks as normal. `!turf cargo` shows what's on the road now, or what's building up if nothing has left yet. This is the valve that keeps PAT moving — what the room spends becomes what the room can steal.

entries.title: !heist [job]
entries.summary: Rob a target, D&D-style — a multi-round survival gauntlet with your !sheet stats, gear, and gang.
entries.details:
Rob a target, D&D-style — a multi-round survival gauntlet with your `!sheet` stats, gear, and gang. Each round everyone rolls 1d20 + a random stat's modifier vs a rising difficulty (plus crew/flawless/gang bonuses). Survive to bank loot, `!bail` to walk away, get pinched and your loot is split among the survivors.
**The vault door:** the casino and bank jobs end at **one shared roll for the whole crew**, made by whoever's best placed for the stat it tests. Open it and the crew splits a slice of the vault — usually a few percent, occasionally a huge haul (up to 40% of the vault, very rarely). Fail it and **everyone at the door loses the loot they were holding** (it stays in the vault) — unless a ⚖️ Good Lawyer saves half. So the last `!bail` window, right before the door, is the big decision: walk away with your loot, or risk it for the vault.
**Odds:** the door is hard on purpose — even a perfect sheet with a full kit opens the casino door only about a third of the time solo, and the Federal Reserve's under 1 in 10; an ordinary sheet still has a real long shot. The bank pays **4× more loot per round** than the casino to make up for it.
**Jobs** (**!heist <job>**, or **!heist list**): 🏪 **store** — small, quick, always open, and a clean getaway can swipe a heist-shop item from the back room (about 1 in 4 robbers, more solo or with a flawless crew, 3 a day); 🎰 **casino** — 5,000 to join, 9 rounds + the door (needs a 100k+ jackpot); 🚚 **convoy** — rob a gang's cargo run (needs a casino job first; it pays out of the cargo itself); 🏛️ **bank** — 20,000 to join, 11 rounds + the door, the legendary Federal Reserve (needs 📐 Blueprints and a casino job, 500k+ vault). Vault jobs are paced by your **own heat** — everyone in the crew takes it, not just the starter — plus a **cooldown per job type** (store 30m, casino 2h, bank 8h) that now survives Pepe restarting. Round loot and the vault slice both scale with the vault, so a fat vault is worth more to everyone. Deep runs can drop rare scores: 📐 Blueprints (unlocks the bank), 🎲 **Loaded Dice** (`!reroll` a stat), 💍 **Kingpin's Ring** (`!ring` +1 a stat), 📈 **The Fence** (+10% payouts), and 🧠 **Mastermind** (advantage on your two best stats). Gear up with `!shop`. See **/heist** for the guide.
**Your loot is real:** what you bank each round is set aside from the vault as you win it, so you always walk out with it. If the vault can't cover a round, Pepe says so — nat 20s get paid first and the rest split what's left.
**Other rooms:** you can `!join` a heist from any room, but the rounds — and `!bail` — only work in the room it's running in.
**Watch it live:** publicaccess.tv/gtf/heist shows the heist running now - the overlay from Pepe's stream, the crew (in, pinched, bailed and what they hold) and everything that happened. Pepe posts the link when a heist starts; the GTF minimap links it too.

entries.title: !invade [area]
entries.summary: Raid a rival gang's borough that borders one of yours.
entries.details: Raid a rival gang's borough that **borders** one of yours. **No turf yet?** You can raid any **outer** borough (Croydon, Brixton, Peckham, Hackney, Tottenham, Camden) for a foothold, even when the whole map is held — mid and center still need a border. Opens a muster window — your gang `!join`s the crew while the defenders `!defend`. The crew rolls through the stash's defence DC ladder; crack it to **seize the stake and flip the borough**, or get repelled. Same tier-rep gates as claiming. (Pepe pulls on a balaclava for the raid. 🏴)

entries.title: !room [room]
entries.summary: Room turf wars: gangs control the pads themselves - bond a free room, raid a held one, pick its perks.
entries.details: After London's last season, turf wars move to the **rooms**. `!room` shows the map: every pad busy enough to fight over (30-day pad-vault inflow of 10,000 PAT a day or more), its tier, its **bond** (20 days of its inflow, 500k to 20M) and who holds it. `!claim <room>` bonds a **free** room from your gang treasury (boss or officers). Holding a room costs **upkeep** every day (8% of its 7-day inflow, at least 3,000), paid **into the room's own vault**, and pays the gang its slice of the room (15% of a tenth of the vault, capped at a quarter of its inflow) - big slices travel on a **convoy** that anyone in the room can try to `!hijack`. `!invade <room>` raids a held room: your crew `!join`s (20k each, into the pad's vault win or lose), the holders `!defend`; win and you post your own bond, the old holder loses 25% of theirs into the vault and gets 75% back. Rooms are locked 72 h after they change hands. Pick 2 perks (3 in the busiest rooms) with `!room perks`: autoshop, fightclub, gunstore, warehouse, bunker, dispensary. `!room release` gives 72 h notice and returns the whole bond. Miss upkeep twice and the room is neglected (easier to raid); let the bond fall behind its recomputed size for a week and it is exposed.

entries.title: !hit / !hijack
entries.summary: Hit a payout convoy - typed in the room it left from, once a day, if you've been there 30 minutes today.
entries.details: With convoys on, a room payout or a gang's daily slice of 25,000 PAT or more leaves on a **convoy** for 10 minutes, announced in the room. `!hit` (or `!hijack`; `!hit convoy` if you're also at a blackjack table) musters a crew that others `!join` (5,000 buy-in each). To crew you need to be **in that room** and to have been there **30 minutes today**, with a PATV account linked to your chat login that is at least **14 days old and level 3+**, not flagged as an alt - and you can't hit a convoy carrying your own payout or your own gang's slice. One attempt a day. The gang that controls the room can `!defend`. Win and the crew splits up to **20%** of the convoy and gets the buy-ins back - a convoy can only be hit once; lose and the buy-ins go into the pad's vault.

entries.title: !snap <user> [-e <hours>]
entries.summary: Grabs a still from someone's cam and posts a link that expires — 25,000 PAT (admins free).
entries.details:
Grabs a still from someone's cam and posts a **link that expires** — **25,000 PAT** (admins free). The default life is **24 hours**; once it's up the image is deleted and the link is dead. Shorten it for one shot with `-e` (`!snap moxier -e 2` = two hours; 5 minutes minimum, 7 days maximum). A copy is also saved on the bot machine, which the expiry doesn't touch.

Unlike `!look` this leaves a picture on the web, so it ships **switched off** and each room opts in — while it's off, only admins can use it. **Room mods switch it** by typing `!snap on` / `!snap off` in that room (`enable` / `disable` work too; mods = Pepe admins, the room's owner and its red list); `!snap status` shows it for anyone. The same switch gates the website's stage snaps and clips of Pepe's stream. To snap someone actually named "on", write `!snap @on`. Needs the cam window (see `!activeroom`).

web.label: Or click the 📷 next to someone on cam on the pad page

entries.title: !clip <user> [-t <secs>] [-e <hours>] [-na | -ao]
entries.summary: Same as !snap but a short video — 50,000 PAT (admins free).
entries.details:
Same as `!snap` but a short **video** — **50,000 PAT** (admins free). Records **40 seconds** by default; `-t` sets the length up to **60s** (`!clip moxier -t 30`). Pepe posts "recording X for 40s…" in the room before he starts. Same **24-hour** expiry as a snap, same `-e` to shorten it, same local copy kept on the bot machine. Aliases `!rec`, `!record`.

**Sound is on by default** — the room's audio is recorded into the clip. Two things have to be true, or it records silently and says which failed: the room must be the one Pepe is listening to (see `!audioroom` — the loopback carries one room at a time), and **someone must be on the mic**. `-na` (or `-mute`) records video only; `-ao` records **sound only** — an audio clip of whoever's on the mic, with its own player page.

Clips are downscaled and compressed to stay postable; if someone's cam is too busy to fit even at the smallest setting, Pepe says so and refunds rather than posting a broken link. Ships **switched off** per room like `!snap`: room mods type `!clip on` / `!clip off` there (`!clip status` for anyone); the website's 🎬 Clip follows the same switch. `!clip @on` clips a user named "on".

web.label: Or click the 📷 next to someone on cam on the pad page, then Clip

entries.title: !autoclip <user> [-n count] [-t secs] [-na | -ao]
entries.summary: Clips them when they take the mic in this room — one clip per mic-up, and -n 5 pre-pays five (up to 20).
entries.details: Clips them when they **take the mic** in this room — one clip per mic-up, and `-n 5` pre-pays five (up to 20). Same options and price per clip as `!clip`, paid up front; unused clips are **refunded** if you `!autoclip cancel <user>` or a day goes by without one being taken. Running it again for the same person adds more. A clip is never used up on a re-grab while one is still recording, or within a minute of the last. `!autoclip list` shows what's left. Admins can add `-always` to clip them on every mic-up until cancelled.

entries.title: !clipmic [@user | N]
entries.summary: Post the audio of a recent mic-up to the room's pad, with its transcript - 500 PAT, 40% to the people heard.
entries.details:
Pepe keeps the last few **mic-ups** of the room he's listening to (the last 30 per room, up to **15 minutes**). `!clipmic` posts the **last** one to the room's pad as an audio post, with its transcript as the caption; `!clipmic @user` posts that person's last mic-up; `!clipmic 3` merges the last 3 (up to 5). It follows the room's `!clip` switch (admins can still use it while it's off) and costs **500 PAT** (its own price, `clipmic`; admins free) - refunded if posting fails. **40%** of it goes to the people heard in the clip (a likeness royalty, paid by the website after a 24 h hold). Anyone who typed `!likeness clips off` can't be clipped.

Never anyone who is `!incognito` or typed `!bridge hide`: Pepe doesn't keep their audio at all. Anyone heard in a posted clip can tap **Remove me** on it on the website.

**Pepe's own mic-ups** count too: when he speaks on the mic (TTS replies, `!say`, DJ drops, spoken announcements) `!clipmic @pepe` clips his last line, and the website's 🔊 Clip works on his 🎙 lines. Only his TTS voice is kept - never music (Spotify), sound effects or jingles. Admins: `!clipmic status`, `!clipmic pepe on|off`.

entries.details: **Kill a snap or clip link before it expires.** `!snap list` shows every live capture — stills and video together, so there's one place to take anything down. It lists — id, whose cam, who took it, which room, and how long it has left. `!snap delete <id>` takes that one down immediately; `!snap delete all` clears every live link at once. `!unsnap <id>` is the short form. Deleting removes the hosted image only — the local copy on the bot machine stays. If the site can't be reached the bot says so explicitly rather than reporting a delete that didn't happen.

Let chatty mode glance at a user's cam for context when seeing it would improve a reply — no command needed, and used sparingly. In the room Pepe's window is on he's told exactly who is on cam; in **other** rooms the roster can't be read (it comes from the window), so he isn't given a list — he can still look at someone actually being talked about, and the window switches to that room for the glance and straight back.

**`!chattycam switch on|off`** controls whether a glance may move the window to this room at all (per room, on by default). Turn it off for a room that's happy for commands to pull the window over but not an idle glance nobody asked for — Pepe then only looks there when it's already the active room. It also needs auto-switch on for that room, and never overrides a room pinned with `!activeroom`. Costs a vision call each time.

Once per quiet spell. Per room, also in the admin panel's Chatty section.

entries.title: !dj on|off
entries.summary: Put Pepe on the decks — he auto-DJs, generating an eclectic set on the fly: crowd-pleasers, deep cuts, every era and genre, no repeats.
entries.details: Put Pepe on the decks — he **auto-DJs**, generating an eclectic set on the fly: crowd-pleasers, deep cuts, every era and genre, no repeats. He **reads the room** — the songs you `!queue` become cues for what he lines up next. He'll even **drop a spoken DJ line over the intro** of some tracks (ducking the music under his voice) — toggle with **!dj talk on/off** (**per room** — add **-all** or **-global** to widen it; **!dj talk chance <0-100>** sets how often). The DJ only speaks up in rooms actually hearing the set — the ones with **!mic music on** — and holds the drop entirely if any of them has DJ talk switched off, since the mic carries one stream to all of them. **!dj next** cues one now, **!dj genre <g>** nudges the vibe, **!dj min <1-5>** sets how many picks stay queued ahead, **!dj status** shows what's going on. **!dj clear** resets the session for a fresh direction: the vibe, his cues and lined-up picks, and everything waiting in the queue (his picks and listeners' requests — paid requests are refunded; Spotify can't delete from its queue, so those tracks are skipped silently when they come up). The current song plays out and the DJ stays on, waiting for a new `!dj vibe` (up to 3 minutes) before he lines anything else up. **Anyone can steer him:** `!dj vibe <what you want>` (e.g. `!dj vibe 90s hip hop`) — or just say it: "pepe play some chill stuff". He leans the set that way for the next ~45 minutes. He also builds on what's actually in the queue right now, so his picks flow on from your requests instead of duplicating them. **Patter mode (one voice on the mic):** while he DJs a room with DJ talk on, everything he'd otherwise say on the mic by himself — welcome-backs for people who join, chatty mic-ups, conversation starters and shout-outs — goes into one short spoken link between songs (over the next intro, music ducked), built from what happened during the song; five people joining is one "welcome in…", not five clips. Questions to him still get a text reply right away. When nothing happened he may open a topic the room is into (or a light headline). Admins tune it with `!dj patter on|off · every <n> · words <n> · joins|starters|chatty on|off · budget <n>`. **Shout-outs:** `!dj shoutout <name> [message] [-d]` (or `!shoutout`) — the DJ names them in his next link; `-d` dedicates the next song. 2,500 PAT, held when you ask and only taken when he says it (refunded if he hasn't within 30 minutes; `!dj shoutout cancel` to undo) — it's split like other paid room commands: by default 20% to the vault of the room it was played in, 10% to the room's owner and the rest to the Federal Reserve. One every 15 minutes per person; keep it friendly — no links, and people who are incognito can't be named.

entries.title: !roomvibe [type|roasts|notes|lock|unlock|refresh|reset]
entries.summary: How Pepe fits in this room: its type, its tone and whether roasts are welcome.
entries.details: Pepe keeps the same personality in every room but adapts his tone to each one. He learns a room's vibe in the background from its chat, mic, topic and pad description. Anyone can see it. The room's admins (red list) can set the room type, whether he may roast people unprompted, and notes he should follow. Setting a type also locks the vibe: `lock` freezes it so Pepe never relearns or changes it (he still refreshes the room notes and regulars), `unlock` lets him keep learning. A pad marked 18+ on publicaccess.tv makes the room an adult room unless the vibe is locked. `refresh` re-learns it now and `reset` clears everything, the lock included, and goes back to what he learned.

entries.title: !modfines on|off · exempt add|remove|list · strikes [user] · appeal <user>
entries.summary: PAT fines for abusing mod powers, per room — for rooms where Pepe isn't allowed to moderate.
entries.details: **PAT fines for abusing mod powers**, per room — for rooms where Pepe isn't allowed to moderate. Kicks, bans, mic-blocks, mutes and demotions are judged the same way as the automod: a block is fine when the mic was the problem (hogging, no sound, distorted, the room complaining), and everything else goes to the AI judge, which rules it justified when in doubt. entries.title: !casino backend on|off|status · all on|off|status
entries.summary: Switch this room's blackjack and Hold'em to the publicaccess.tv casino backend, where web players can sit at the same table.
entries.details: Switch **this room's** blackjack and Hold'em between Pepe's own tables and the **publicaccess.tv casino backend**. With the backend on, `!bj` / `!holdem` and their verbs (`!bet`, `!hit`, `!stand`, `!double`, `!split`, `!insurance`, `!autobet`, `!sit`, `!check`, `!call`, `!raise`, `!allin`, `!fold`, `!cards`, `!leave`) play a table that lives on the site: the same rules, and signed-in web players can sit at it too (Pepe posts the table's link when it opens, and each round's shuffle proof when it ends; `!bj fair` / `!holdem fair` repeats it). Hold'em hole cards come by PM. A web table's host can push it into the room, and onto Pepe's stream (one table at a time: first come, then a queue). It refuses to switch while an old table is still open here. **status** says which one the room uses (anyone can ask). **all on** / **all off** switch every room Pepe is in at once (rooms with an old table still open are skipped and keep what they play on) and set the **new rooms default**, so rooms Pepe joins later follow it; **default on|off** changes only that default (the rooms he is in keep what they play on now). **all status** lists every room. On a Pepe with no publicaccess.tv site set up, **on** is refused and every table stays Pepe's own. The same switches are in Pepe's admin panel (Website & Feed → Backends).

entries.title: !backend status · !backends
entries.summary: See where every publicaccess.tv backend switch stands: the casino per room, the lotto, stashes, GTF records, pools, polls, gangs, the escrow and the capital cluster (markets, Reserve loans, vaults).
entries.details: **status** (or `!backends`) lists every switch in one line: where each feature runs (Pepe or publicaccess.tv), anything frozen or in conflict, how many rooms play the casino on the site, and whether the site answers (anyone can ask). **all on|off** (admins) switches the per-room switches in every room Pepe is in, which today means the casino (the same as `!casino backend all on|off`). It never moves the one-way hand-overs: the lotto, stashes, GTF records, pools, polls, gangs, the escrow (ledger and games) and the capital cluster (markets, Reserve loans, vaults) each move with their own command (`!lotto backend …`, `!stash backend …`, `!gtf backend …`, `!econ pools backend …`, `!poll backend …`, `!gang backend …`, `!escrow backend …`, `!capital backend …`), one at a time. Pepe's admin panel has the same view (Website & Feed → Backends).

entries.title: !gtf backend on|off|status
entries.summary: Move Grand Theft Frogger's records (heist sheets, loadouts, avatars, duel / brawl / arena records, vault cracks) to publicaccess.tv, or bring them back into Pepe.
entries.details: **on** hands GTF's records to the publicaccess.tv GTF backend (the site must have it enabled too). Pepe pauses GTF commands for a moment once no heist, arena, raid or fight is running, sends everything with a checksum and totals, and switches only when the site confirms the same totals. From then on his files are a local copy and every change goes up to the site; the heist and raid engines stay in Pepe. **off** is the way back: last changes go up, the site freezes its copy and hands everything back, and Pepe writes it into his own files again. **off force** goes back to Pepe's local copy without asking the site (only if the site lost the data). **status** says where the records live and how many changes are waiting to sync (anyone can ask).

entries.title: !gang backend status|export|cutover|rollback|detach
entries.summary: Move the gangs (members, ranks, allowances, upgrades, war records, treasuries and rep) to publicaccess.tv, or bring them back into Pepe.
entries.details: **export** is the dry run: what would move, with totals, and anything that blocks it (the pools must already live on the site; no withdrawal, disband payout or season close may still be paying; nothing running). **cutover confirm** pauses gang commands for a moment, sends every gang and member (each with their PATV account) with a checksum and totals, and switches only when the site confirms the same totals; from then on every gang change is a site transaction and the games (heists, raids, claims, the turf tick) stay in Pepe. **rollback confirm** is the way back while the site answers: every treasury comes back under one key and Pepe owns the gangs again. **detach confirm** is only for a site that is gone for good: Pepe's last copy becomes the truth. **status** says where the gangs live (anyone can ask).

entries.title: !capital backend status|export|cutover|rollback|detach
entries.summary: Move the share markets, the Federal Reserve's loans and the staking vaults to publicaccess.tv together, or bring them back into Pepe.
entries.details: The prediction markets (shares and their pots), the Federal Reserve's loans to players (requests, limits, collection, the credit history) and the staking vaults (the share book, the stake / unstake queue and the daily 04:00 UTC cut-off) move **together**: the Bank's value includes the loans still out and the Market maker's the markets it seeded, so the share prices are only right where all three live. **export** is the dry run: what would move, with totals and the vaults' values, and anything that blocks it (the pools and stashes must already live on the site; nothing may be settling, being funded or mid-move; not within 20 minutes of the 04:00 UTC cut-off). **cutover confirm** pauses these commands for a moment, sends everything with a checksum and totals, and switches only when the site confirms the same totals, the same vault values to the PAT and the same shares; from then on every trade, loan and stake is a site transaction (also from the website, without Pepe), and Pepe announces them. **rollback confirm** is the way back while the site answers. **detach confirm** is only for a site that is gone for good: Pepe's last copy becomes the truth. **status** says where they live (anyone can ask). `!market backend`, `!loan backend` and `!staking backend` are the same command.

entries.title: !econ engines status|export|cutover|rollback|detach
entries.summary: Hand the economy's clock-driven policy engines (the treasury's Monday waterfall and daily release, the monetary day, the burn accrual) to publicaccess.tv's scheduler, or bring them back into Pepe.
entries.details: Three engines, one switch each: **treasury** (the Monday 04:00 UTC surplus waterfall and the daily 04:00 release), **monetary** (the Fed band's floor mint and ceiling release, the Monday guarantee, issuance, the daily activity rewards) and **burn** (the burn reserve's accrual burn). Pepe runs an engine only while its switch is explicitly off; with it on he never runs it, even if the site is down (the site runs the period when it is back). Before a cutover the site runs the engine as a **dry run** (it records what would move) and then in **shadow** (it plans alongside Pepe every period and compares his plan with its own; admins set those on /admin/economy). **export** is the dry run of the hand-over: what Pepe would hand over (the periods he already ran, when his ticks were armed) and anything that blocks it (not within 20 minutes of 04:00 UTC, nothing mid-move here, the pools and the share book already on the site, the engine in shadow there). **cutover confirm** stops the engine here first, then the site takes it and runs every period from then on (one transaction per period, never twice); what it does is written into Pepe's own books as it happens (the epoch and day records, mints, Fed loan repayments, budget spends, burns) and Pepe still announces burns and tells admins about cap notices and failures. **rollback confirm** is the way back while the site answers (it goes back to shadow); **detach confirm** only when the site is gone for good (Pepe runs again from the next period boundary). **status** says where each engine runs (anyone can ask). Admin mints, Fed grants and loans, flash liquidity and donation mints have their own switch (`!econ fed backend`); the room payout recipe and the launchpad stay in Pepe.

entries.title: !econ fed backend status|export|on|off|detach
entries.summary: Hand the Federal Reserve's one-off operations (admin mints, grants, Fed loans, flash liquidity, donation mints) and their books to publicaccess.tv, or bring them back into Pepe.
entries.details: The Fed's **event operations** - `!econ mint`, `!econ fund`, `!econ fedloan` (and its early repayment), flash liquidity, the Bank's default backstop, restore and seed mints, the donation mints - and their books (every mint, grant and loan, the monthly mint caps, the Fed band) move to the site as one: from then on the site checks the caps and the band, moves the PAT and writes the journal in **one transaction per operation**, so a monthly cap can never be passed by two mints landing at once (the site's scheduler mints through the same book). The commands keep their dry runs, confirms and texts; Pepe's copy of the journal becomes a read-only mirror (`!econ mints`, `!econ fedloan`, the admin card read it as before). **export** is the dry run: the journal's totals and checksum, checked by the site without changing anything (needs the pools and the share book already on the site, the economy layers on, nothing half-done here). **on** freezes the Fed's operations for a moment, sends the journal with a checksum and totals and switches only when the site confirms them with the supply unchanged. **off** is the way back while the site answers; **detach confirm** only when the site is gone for good (Pepe's mirror becomes his journal again). With the switch on and the site down an admin operation is refused - never written locally - and a booking whose PAT already moved (a weekly loan repayment, a Bank repayment of a flash loan) waits and is sent again. **status** says where the Fed's books live (anyone can ask).

entries.title: !aijudge backend status|on|off
entries.summary: Make Pepe's AI judge propose its calls to publicaccess.tv, which runs the dispute window and settles, or let him decide locally again.
entries.details: With **on**, Pepe still looks into AI-judged markets, betting pools and wagers (web search plus his own chat records) but only PROPOSES a result to the site, with his confidence, his reason and the evidence. The site keeps the proposal and the disputes, and when the dispute window ends without enough disputes it settles the items it runs itself; the ones that still live in Pepe are settled by him when the site says so. `!market dispute` / `!wager dispute` go to the site. If the site is down, his calls wait and nothing is settled. **off** brings the dispute window back to Pepe (calls already made settle on their own window). **status** says which way it runs (anyone can ask).

entries.title: !cosmetics backend status|on|off
entries.summary: Move the cosmetic drop table (every win's drop chance, the daily cap, the gates) to publicaccess.tv, or bring it back to Pepe's panel.
entries.details: **on confirm** hands Pepe's drop table to the site once; from then on it is edited on the site's admin page (Cosmetics) and Pepe reads it every 5 minutes, still rolling the drops for in-chat games himself (the site rolls the wheel's and the casino tables' drops with the same numbers). If the site is down he keeps using the last copy. **off confirm** brings the site's numbers back as Pepe's drop knobs. **status** says where the table lives (anyone can ask).

entries.title: !achievements backend status|export|on|off|detach
entries.summary: Move the chat achievement counters to publicaccess.tv (the site then checks the thresholds and awards), or bring them back into Pepe.
entries.details: **export** is the dry run: how many people, unlocks and counters would move, with a checksum, and anything that blocks it. **on confirm** pauses awards for a moment, sends every counter with a checksum and totals, checks every person's copy on the site and switches only when they all match; from then on Pepe still counts what happens in the rooms and sends it to the site, which checks the thresholds and pays the badge, XP and points once (Pepe announces it in the room). **off confirm** is the way back while the site answers: everything waiting is sent first, then the counters come back exactly. **detach confirm** is only for a site that is gone for good: Pepe's last copy becomes the counters again. **status** says where the counters live (anyone can ask).

entries.title: !automod [action] [user]

`!automod remove [action] [user]` — remove a specific rule

entries.title: !pepefeed [status|on|off|now]
entries.summary: Pepe on the website feed.
entries.details:
**Pepe on the website feed.** On publicaccess.tv Pepe answers when someone mentions him in a pad (`@pepe` in a post or comment), and where a pad allows it he chimes in on fresh posts or makes the odd post of his own. He can look at pictures in posts (he describes them but never guesses who a person is), and never touches NSFW posts. `!pepefeed` (or `status`) shows whether he's on, the last sync, the last 24 h of posts and comments, and today's feed spend. `!pepefeed off` is the **bot-side kill switch**: he stops reading and writing on the feed entirely (it survives restarts); `!pepefeed on` turns him back on. `!pepefeed now` checks the feed straight away instead of waiting for the next round. Example: `!pepefeed off` if he's misbehaving on the site.

The day-to-day settings (mentions, chiming in, limits, quiet hours, pictures) live on the website: site-wide in Feed admin, per pad in the pad's moderation page (owners). Those still apply while this switch is on. Not the same as `!promo`, which is house ads in chat.

entries.title: !automkt [status|on|off|now|preview|list|approve|reject|count|mode|cat|trending|polls]
syntax: !automkt [cat sports|prices|news|trending on|off | trending on|off | polls on|off | polyevery <h> | pollhours <h>]
entries.summary: Pepe's auto markets: markets and pools he opens himself about real-world events.
entries.details:
**Auto markets.** Pepe opens a few prediction markets and betting pools a week by himself about real-world events: **sports** fixtures (who wins, from ESPN's scoreboard: NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, Premier League, UFC), **prices** (will Bitcoin / the S&P 500 be above a round level at a set time, from Coinbase / Yahoo Finance) and **news** (clear yes/no questions written from BBC and NPR headlines). Each one has exact resolution criteria, a source link, a close time BEFORE the event starts and a resolution time, and is tagged 🤖 auto on [/markets](https://publicaccess.tv/markets). Sports and prices settle from the same data source; news questions go to Pepe's AI judge with the criteria. Postponed, cancelled or unreadable ones are voided (pools refund every stake) or handed to the admins. Markets are seeded by the Market maker vault like any other (a weekly cap; no seed = a yes/no pool instead), and never about deaths, violence, elections, private people, adult or illegal topics, or anything players could influence.

`!automkt` shows the status; `on` / `off` switches it (off by default); `now [n]` makes n right away; `preview` shows what's next without creating anything; `list` the review queue and the latest; `approve <id>` / `reject <id> [why]` the ones waiting for review (by default news questions wait for an admin's OK); `count <n>` = how many a week; `mode news|all|none` = which ones need review; `cat sports|prices|news on|off`.

**Trending** (off by default; `!automkt trending on|off`): Pepe looks at the busiest topics on Polymarket's public data a few times a day and uses them as IDEAS only - he writes his own question, his own resolution criteria and date and links an official source (never a prediction-market site); anything too close to their wording, or about politics, war, people's health, minors or anything else off-limits, is thrown away. Trending ones wait for review like news ones. Pepe never opens a market AND a pool (or a poll) about the same topic: he checks every live market, pool and poll and remembers recent topics for 30 days. The type fits the question: yes/no = a market, one winner out of several = a pool, an opinion = a room poll (`!automkt polls on|off`, one at a time, open `pollhours` hours), mixed so the feed isn't all one kind. `polyevery <h>` = how often the trending list is refreshed (default 6 h). `weight <category> <0-10>` sets the mix (0 = never; sports is low by default), `marquee on|off` keeps sports to finals, championships, the postseason and numbered UFC cards (no single regular matches - on by default), and `pad <pad id>|default` picks the pad they all go to (default: Pepe's Pad). Each one closes at (15 minutes before) its event, never days earlier. Every announcement links to the item's page. The same controls are in the admin panel (Games, **Auto markets**) and on the website at /admin/markets.

entries.title: !mic tts on|off · voice · model · engine · chatty
entries.summary: Configure Pepe's voice.
entries.details: Configure Pepe's voice. **on/off** enables TTS; **voice <name>** sets the default voice (list them with **!mic tts voices**, which is public); **model <1.7B|0.6B|1B|3B>** and **engine <name>** switch the TTS model; **chatty <0-100>** sets how often Pepe mics up his chat lines instead of typing them; **caption on/off** also posts the text when he mics up, and a soundboard clip's line as it plays (for accessibility; ON by default); **test [text]** speaks a test line.

entries.title: !mic grab · force · lock · drop · slots
entries.summary: Pepe's own mic control.
entries.details:
Pepe's own mic control. **grab/hold** takes & holds a mic (re-grabs when a slot frees); **force** seizes a slot even when the mic's full; **lock self,alice,…** restricts the mic to named users (everyone else is blocked) and **unlock** lifts it; **drop** lets go; **slots <n>** sets the room's mic-slot limit.
**Per room:** every room has its own mic button, so holding, hold-mode and force-mode all belong to one room — Pepe can be holding the mic for music in one room while free in another, and stepping into a room to speak one line no longer makes him keep its mic. `!mic drop` lets go of the room you're in (and says where else he's still holding); `!mic drop all` lets go **everywhere**. `!mic status` lists the other rooms he's holding in.
**Scope of a settings command:** `!mic music off`, `!mic tts voice X`, `!mic alerts`, `!mic slots`, `!mic tts on|off|chatty|caption` all change **the room you typed them in** (like `!redlist`). Add `-global` to change the default that rooms without their own setting follow — rooms that do override it are unaffected, and Pepe says so. Add `-all` to change the default and clear every room's override, so every room really gets it.
**Random voice:** set any voice to `random` — `!mic tts voice random`, `!say … -v random`, or the room/alert voice in the panel — and Pepe picks a different one every line. It only ever picks voices that are free for whoever asked, so it can never bill you for a premium voice you didn't choose (admins, who use every voice free, get the full range).
**Per-room settings:** each room can also have its own default voice, chatty-voice frequency, caption/alert switches, jukebox-on-mic setting and mic-slot limit — set them in the admin panel with that room selected. Chat commands like `!mic tts voice` set the global default that rooms without an override follow. The VoiceBox engine, model size and audio device stay global, since there's only one of each.

entries.title: !mic reset
entries.summary: Recovery tool.
entries.details: **Recovery tool.** Makes Pepe forget what he thinks he's holding, in every room — and deliberately **clicks nothing**, so it can't make the client worse. Use it when a room is stuck showing held that `!mic drop` won't clear: dropping a mic that isn't really on would turn it on, so once his belief and the client disagree there's otherwise no way back. Afterwards check the client and use **!mic grab** / **!mic drop** to line them up. (Aliases: **!mic resync**, **!mic forget**.)

entries.title: !mic status · device · test
entries.summary: status shows everything at once — hold mode, whether the audio pipeline is armed, whether Pepe holds a slot, who else is on the mic, any lock or force-block, and the output device.
entries.details: **status** shows everything at once — hold mode, whether the audio pipeline is armed, whether Pepe holds a slot, who else is on the mic, any lock or force-block, and the output device. **device <name>** sets that output device by substring (e.g. `!mic device CABLE Input`); with no name it just tells you the current one. **test** plays a tone to it, grabbing the mic if needed — the quickest way to check the audio path end to end.

entries.title: !mic force audio on|off
entries.summary: Lets Pepe interrupt a full mic to play a clip — a !say, an alert sting, or a chatty mic-up.
entries.details: Lets Pepe **interrupt a full mic to play a clip** — a `!say`, an alert sting, or a chatty mic-up. When it's on and every slot is taken, he bumps whoever's on, plays the clip, then **drops and unblocks them straight away**. He does not keep the mic, which is what makes this different from plain **!mic force** (that seizes a slot and holds it). Off (the default) he just waits for a slot to free up, and a clip is only dropped if the mic stays full for the whole wait. Handy in a busy room where Pepe would otherwise never get a word in; rude if you leave it on during a serious conversation.

entries.title: !mic click · pipeline
entries.summary: Resync tools for the rare case where Pepe's mic state drifts (he's really on the mic but thinks he's off, so drop does nothing).
entries.details: Resync tools for the rare case where Pepe's mic state drifts (he's really on the mic but thinks he's off, so **drop** does nothing). **click** (aliases **resync**/**kick**) fires a raw mic-button click without changing his tracked state — it physically toggles the real mic so you can nudge hardware and belief back into agreement, then use grab/drop normally. **pipeline** also clicks but flips the tracked arm/disarm flag with it.

entries.title: !mic alerts on|off · music on|off
entries.summary: alerts switches the alert sound channel on or off for this room — the full alert controls are under !alerts.
entries.details: **alerts** switches the alert sound channel on or off for this room — the full alert controls are under `!alerts`. **music** makes Pepe hold the mic while the jukebox plays so the whole room hears it.

entries.title: !alerts
entries.summary: How big moments — a heist forming, a turf invasion, the jackpot cracking, a big win — reach each room.
entries.details:
How big moments — a **heist** forming, a **turf invasion**, the **jackpot** cracking, a **big win** — reach each room. An alert is an event, not a sound: it can arrive by any combination of **three channels**, each switched separately.

**Channels (per room):** `!alerts sound on|off` a sting through the mic · `!alerts tts on|off` Pepe says it out loud · `!alerts text on|off` a line in chat. `!alerts on|off` is the master switch — off and this room gets nothing at all. Like every settings command these change **the room you typed them in**; add `-global` or `-all` to widen.

**Scope (per event, global):** `!alerts heist room` keeps a heist alert in the room it started in. `!alerts heist global` also tells every other room where it's kicking off, by tab name — "a heist is forming in Pepe's Pad". A room with alerts switched off stays quiet either way, so one room can opt out of the noise entirely.

**Voice:** `!alerts voice <name>` gives spoken alerts their own voice in this room, so an alert cuts through instead of sounding like everything else Pepe says. `!alerts voice random` re-rolls one each time, `!alerts voice default` goes back to the room's usual voice. Per room, like the channels.

**Force the mic:** `!alerts jackpot force on` lets that alert **bump whoever is on the mic** so the sting or spoken line actually gets heard, rather than queueing and being dropped if no slot frees up. It cuts someone off mid-sentence, so it's set per event and off by default — worth it for the jackpot, rarely for anything else. Text alerts never need a mic slot and are unaffected.

**Notes:** spoken alerts need TTS on in that room — if it's off they simply don't play there, whatever this is set to. The text channel doesn't repeat itself in the room the event happened in (that room already posts its own announcement); it writes the "it's happening over there" line into the other rooms. `!alerts test <type>` fires one to check your setup, and `!alerts` on its own shows where everything stands. All of it is in the admin panel too.
