entries.summary: List the participant list's real usernames (recovered from Camfrog's owner-drawn list).
entries.details: List the participant list's real usernames (recovered from Camfrog's owner-drawn list).

entries.title: !promo [on|off|now|list] · every · cap · msgs · vary · skip
entries.summary: House ads in chat.
entries.details:
**House ads in chat.** Pepe now and then posts a short line advertising his own games and features (a free `!sponsor` for the house). Off by default. `!promo on|off` switches it for the room you type it in; add `-global` for rooms without their own setting, or `-all` for every room. `!promo` alone shows the status here: on or off, today's count, when the last ad went out and what it's waiting for.

It stays quiet by design: one ad slot per room, **shared with sponsors** (paid sponsors always go first), only while the room is actually talking, never during a game, heist, casino table or lotto draw, never with two or more people on the mic, and the same ad never twice in a room within 24 h.

Settings (all rooms): `!promo every <15-720>` minutes between ads (default 50) · `!promo cap <0-24>` house ads per room per day (default 4) · `!promo msgs <n>` chat lines needed since the last ad (default 15) · `!promo vary on|off` lets the AI reword a line (it keeps every !command and link). `!promo list` shows the ads; `!promo skip <id>` / `unskip <id>` mutes one. `!promo now` tries one here immediately (still skips anything not allowed right now, and says why). Example: `!promo on` then `!promo every 90`. Not the same as `!pepefeed`, which is Pepe on the website feed.

entries.title: !chatty on/off/status
entries.summary: Toggle chatty mode — bot chimes in on conversations unprompted.
entries.details: Toggle chatty mode — bot chimes in on conversations unprompted. Per room: `!chatty on|off` changes the room you type it in; add `-global` to set the default for rooms without their own setting, or `-all` for every room. Chatty frequency (admin panel) is per room the same way, and so is the cooldown: Pepe chiming in in one room doesn't hold him back in another (mentions and follow-ups are always answered).

entries.title: !chattydepth off|short|normal|long · cap <n> · memory <%> [tokens] · end [user]
entries.summary: Chatty depth (per room, default normal): after Pepe answers you, he stays in the conversation for a bit — your next lines that look meant for him get answered without saying "pepe"…
entries.details: **Chatty depth** (per room, default normal): after Pepe answers you, he stays in the conversation for a bit — your next lines that look meant for him get answered without saying "pepe" (short = 3 follow-ups, normal = 6, long = 12; it ends after 1/2/5 quiet minutes, when you say bye/stop, or when the follow-ups run out — saying his name again refreshes them). Lines aimed at someone else (@bob…, bob, …), a bare "lol", or a room that's moved on don't count. Long conversations are summarized in the background so he keeps the thread. `cap` = follow-ups per hour in the room; `memory` = how much of the model's context a conversation fills before it's summarized; `end` stops the conversations in the room. Turns itself down when the daily AI budget runs low.

entries.title: !greeter on|off · stats · new <mode> · regulars <mode> · dwell · away · rejoin · test <user>
entries.summary: Greeter mode (per room): Pepe says hello to people who stay a while - a relaxed shared welcome for newcomers, a short personal hello for regulars - and skips people who already left.
entries.details: **Greeter mode** (per room): nobody is greeted the moment they arrive. Newcomers who stay 90 s (`dwell new`) get one relaxed, shared welcome addressed to the room - everyone new within 30 s shares the line, no @-ping, no questions, nothing on the mic unless `new text+mic` (then a spoken welcome that names nobody). Regulars who stay 20 s (`dwell regular`) get a short personal hello, at most once per person every `away` hours (default 6), never after a quick rejoin (`rejoin`, default 20 min); `regulars mic` speaks a `mic` share (default 25%) when the mic is free right then. Right before greeting, Pepe re-checks they're still in the room; anyone who left, or who already chatted with Pepe, is skipped, and a greeting older than 60 s is dropped (it never waits in the mic queue). At most one greeting per `cooldown` minutes (default 3); a burst of joins or a busy chat skips regulars' hellos. `stats` shows what was sent and skipped since the restart. Saying wb me gets you one on demand.

entries.title: !dms
entries.summary: Read Pepe's Camfrog direct-message inbox (the contact-list message inbox, separate from in-room PMs).
entries.details: **Read Pepe's Camfrog direct-message inbox** (the contact-list message inbox, separate from in-room PMs). Pepe opens the inbox, screenshots it and reads the conversation list — sender, time, preview and unread count — then reports it to you privately. **Read-only:** Pepe can't reply to DMs. Run it whenever you want to check; there's no automatic DM handling.

entries.title: !autotopic on/off/now/status
entries.summary: Toggle auto-topic — bot sets a witty room topic via /topic as the conversation evolves (how often is the Auto-Topic Frequency slider in the admin panel; ~30 min + 30 msgs by default).
entries.details: Toggle auto-topic — bot sets a witty room topic via /topic as the conversation evolves (how often is the Auto-Topic Frequency slider in the admin panel; ~30 min + 30 msgs by default). Per room: `!autotopic on|off` changes the room you type it in; add `-global` to set the default for rooms without their own setting, or `-all` for every room. Each room keeps its own timer, and the frequency is per room the same way. `now` sets a new topic in this room right away (without switching auto-topic on); `status` says whether the room uses its own setting.

entries.title: !cmdswitch
entries.summary: The master switch for any command or feature: off means off in every room, whatever the room or the pad owner set.
entries.details: Every user-facing command and feature has a **master switch** (off = off everywhere) on top of its **global default** (what rooms follow) and each room's own setting. `!cmdswitch` lists what's off; `!cmdswitch !imagine` shows one switch (master, default, this room, the result here); `!cmdswitch !imagine off` turns the master off; `!cmdswitch default !trivia off` changes the default rooms follow; `!cmdswitch ai off` switches every AI command and feature off at once. A switched-off command answers with one short line and charges nothing; passive features (chatty, greetings, the auto-topic...) just stay quiet. Switches bind admins too - they can still use a switched-off command's settings words (on, off, status, cancel...), and `!cmdswitch test on` gives YOU an hour of test mode in which only you can use switched-off commands (Pepe says 🧪 test mode when he lets you through; it ends by itself, `!cmdswitch test off` ends it sooner, and it's logged). The AI model registry's on/off lives here too: every AI model function has its row (or is its feature's own switch). Every change is logged. The full table, with search and bulk actions, is on the website's admin pages (Pepe > Commands).

entries.title: How multiple rooms work
entries.summary: Pepe can sit in several chat rooms at once, and each one is its own place.
entries.details:
Pepe can sit in several chat rooms at once, and each one is its own place.

**People carry over, rooms don't.** What he knows about you follows you between rooms (and he'll say where he heard it — "you mentioned that in the other room"); a room's own lore, chat log and transcripts stay in that room.

**Chat & transcripts are per room.** Anything that quotes history — `!ask`, `!roast`, `!chart`, chatty replies, DJ patter — only draws on the room you're in. So do `!log`, `!replay`, `!search`, `!mictop`, `!micstats` and `!modlog`. Add `-all` to any of those to search or total across every room instead.

**Settings are per room.** Games, chatty, cams and the rest can be switched on in one room and off in another from the admin panel's room selector — only the AI model/API settings are shared.

**Telegram** has its own scope: `/room <name>` focuses a chat on one room, `/room all` widens it. Keyword alerts always cover every room and say which one they came from.

**Voice and cams live in one room at a time** — whichever `!audioroom` / `!activeroom` point at. Mic and cam commands are refused elsewhere with a note saying which room owns them.

entries.title: !audioroom [room] · all
entries.summary: Pick which rooms Pepe listens to: one room (the rest muted) or all of them.
entries.details:
When Pepe is in more than one room, set which room's **audio** is live. Loopback captures a single audio stream, so only the chosen room's mic-ups get recorded/transcribed — the others are skipped to avoid misattributing what was said. `!audioroom` alone shows the current room and the rooms seen; `!audioroom all` (or `off`) records every room. (Alias: `!microom`.)
**Automatic switching:** once the speaker control is recorded with `!audiobtn`, this actually **moves the audio in the client** — mutes the room that currently has it, switches to the target's tab, then unmutes that one, all in the background with no focus stolen. If any step fails the previous room is unmuted again and the setting is left alone, so you never end up with two rooms feeding one stream, or none. Add `-noswitch` to record the setting **without** touching the client — for when the audio is already where you want it and only the bot's idea of it was wrong. (Also `-nomove` / `-setonly`.)
**With net audio on (`!netaudio on`)** Pepe hears every room separately from its own audio connection, so nothing has to be muted for him to transcribe. `!audioroom all` (the default) transcribes **every** room and **unmutes every room's speaker**, so the stream / desktop audio hears them all. Naming rooms works like before: `!audioroom DRAMA_CENTRAL` (or `RoomA, RoomB`) keeps those rooms audible and transcribed and **mutes the others**, which are then not transcribed either; `!audioroom +Room` adds a room (unmuted, transcribed), `-Room` removes one (muted, not transcribed). Muting is always your choice: only `all` unmutes everything. The speaker states are remembered and put back whenever Pepe rejoins a room; a room he joins later follows the current choice. `!audioroom` is one choice for the whole bot, never a per-room setting. The website's room audio (`!bridge audio`) streams **every** bridged room that has it switched on, each from its own audio; with net audio off only the `!audioroom` room can stream (the loopback is one mix).

entries.title: !netaudio [on · off]
entries.summary: Transcribe every room Pepe is in at once, from each room's own audio.
entries.details: Camfrog plays all of Pepe's rooms through one mixed sound stream, which is why `!audioroom` normally has to pick one room. With **net audio** on, Pepe takes each room's voice straight from that room's own audio connection instead, so mic-ups in every room are recorded and transcribed separately, each tagged with its room (and with the person who was actually talking when he can tell). `!clip` sound, mic clips and the website's room audio work per room too. While it is on, the old speaker capture (the loopback) is closed completely; `!audioroom all` then unmutes every room. `!netaudio` shows the state (rooms found, speakers, decode errors, the transcription queue, whether the loopback is open); `on` / `off` switch it. `off` reopens the loopback and, if an `!audioroom` room is set, makes that the one audible room again. Ships **off**.

entries.title: !audiostats [prio on · off] [helper on · off] [latency <s>]
entries.summary: How healthy the audio Pepe broadcasts is: dropouts in his voice and on the virtual mic.
entries.details: Pepe plays his voice (TTS, DJ drops, clips) from a small helper process of its own with a generous buffer, and listens to the virtual mic (what Camfrog sends) for **gaps** - moments of silence cut into music or speech, the sign of a player that fell behind. `!audiostats` shows the voice clips played and their underflows, the gaps heard on the cable (total and the last minute), the process priorities (Camfrog and Spotify are kept above OBS; Pepe himself at normal) and the command worker's queue. Every minute with gaps is logged as `[AUDIO-UNDERRUN]`. `prio off` stops raising Camfrog/Spotify; `helper off` plays the voice inside Pepe again (both remembered; `on` switches them back). It also shows the room-audio settings in force and each streamed room's audio stats. `latency <s>` sets the room mixer's jitter cushion (website room audio and per-room recording) - the same setting as Room audio on the website's admin page (/admin/pepe/audio), where the other room-audio knobs live; it is saved there.

entries.title: !saymod [off · light · standard · strict] [-global]
entries.summary: The !say moderator: keeps repeats, slurs and targeted abuse off Pepe's mic. Off unless a room picks a level.
entries.details: Checks what people have Pepe say out loud (`!say`, `!remind`/`!relay` with `-mic`, soundboard TTS clips) **before anything is charged** - a refused line costs nothing and the sender gets a short reason (never their own words back). Levels: **light** refuses repeats (the same line a third time in 2 min), slurs aimed at someone, threats, doxxing and "kys"; **standard** adds any slur and insults aimed at someone in the room; **strict** adds harsh swearing and, if `llm on`, a cheap AI read of what the word lists let through. Three refusals in 10 minutes pause that person's spoken requests for 15 minutes. `!saymod` shows this room's level; `!saymod <level>` sets it for this room, `-global` for every room without its own; pad owners pick theirs on the owner page. PATV admins have a master switch (the commands page, `say_mod`).

entries.title: !activeroom [room] [force] · auto
entries.summary: When Pepe is in more than one room, set which room's window is targeted by window-driven actions — his own mic button, the participant-list read, and cam opening.
entries.details:
When Pepe is in more than one room, set which room's **window** is targeted by window-driven actions — his own mic button, the participant-list read, and cam opening. **It's also the main-stage room:** the stream shows Pepe's room window, so pinning a room clicks its tab, the publicaccess.tv homepage shows that room as On stage, and its live room page plays the stream above the chat. Only rooms Pepe is in; it waits while a game is running (add `force` to move it anyway); Pepe's mic and music don't block it. Site admins can do the same from the homepage stage. `!activeroom` alone shows the setting; `!activeroom auto` follows whichever tab is open. `!activeroom <tab label>=<room>` tells Pepe which tab belongs to which room when the two are named differently. (Alias: `!winroom`.)

**Auto-switch:** with Auto-switch room tab on in the admin panel, Pepe changes tabs himself instead of refusing — a window-driven command just runs in the room it was typed in. Spoken audio (`!say`, `-mic` replies, sponsor reads) **queues**: the tab is switched immediately before each clip takes the mic, so several people speaking from different rooms play one after another in the right rooms rather than fighting over the tab. Pinning a room with `!activeroom` disables auto-switching.

entries.title: !audiostatus
entries.summary: Reads every room's speaker button and reports which rooms are live, muted, or unknown — and refreshes the mute column in the admin panel's status card.
entries.details: Reads every room's speaker button and reports which rooms are live, muted, or unknown — and refreshes the mute column in the admin panel's status card. On demand only: reading a room's state means switching to its tab, so it is never polled. Rooms show as unknown until Pepe has had reason to look at them; any `!audioroom` move visits them all and fills the picture in. (Alias: `!mutestatus`.)

entries.title: !mute · !unmute [room]
entries.summary: Mutes or unmutes one room's audio in the client without changing the !audioroom setting — the repair tool for when the two drift apart.
entries.details: Mutes or unmutes **one room's audio in the client** without changing the `!audioroom` setting — the repair tool for when the two drift apart. Switches to the room first (a speaker button only exists while its room is on screen), then clicks. If the button reports its state on your build these are **idempotent** (a second `!mute` does nothing); if it doesn't, they act as a plain toggle and say so rather than claiming a state they can't see. (Alias: `!roomaudio`.)

entries.title: !roombuttons
entries.summary: Lists the room window's buttons (control id, position, size) to the bot log — how the speaker/mute control gets identified, the same way the mic button was.
entries.details: Lists the room window's buttons (control id, position, size) to the bot log — how the **speaker/mute** control gets identified, the same way the mic button was. (Alias: `!roombtns`.)

entries.title: !clickbtn [id] [room]
entries.summary: Test-clicks one control by id, in the background.
entries.details: Test-clicks one control by id, in the background. Use it to work out which button mutes a room, then record it with `!audiobtn`. (Alias: `!clickbutton`.)

entries.title: !audiobtn [id]
entries.summary: Records which control mutes/unmutes a room's audio.
entries.details: Records which control mutes/unmutes a room's audio. Once set, **!audioroom <room>** moves the audio itself — mutes the old room, switches tab, unmutes the new one — with no clicking and without Camfrog taking focus. Without an argument it shows the current setting. Stored per install, since the id can differ between Camfrog builds. With no argument it reports the id and whether **state detection** is calibrated. Pepe works out which button reading means "muted" by comparing every open room — the odd one out is the live one — which is what makes `!mute`/`!unmute` idempotent rather than blind toggles. `!audiobtn recal` re-learns it if it ever gets it wrong; it needs at least two rooms open with exactly one unmuted.

entries.title: !roomtabs
entries.summary: Lists the room tabs Pepe can see in the Camfrog window, and which one is currently open.
entries.details: Lists the room **tabs** Pepe can see in the Camfrog window, and which one is currently open. Rooms aren't separate windows — one window swaps contents — so this is what auto-switching actually clicks. (Alias: `!tabs`.)

entries.title: !roomswitch [room]
entries.summary: Switch the Camfrog window to a room's tab, without stealing focus or bringing Camfrog to the front.
entries.details: Switch the Camfrog window to a room's tab, without stealing focus or bringing Camfrog to the front. Reports whether the switch was **verified** (the window title actually changed) — the safe way to test auto-switching before enabling it. A room's tab label and its room id are unrelated strings ("Pepe's Pad" vs "PepeFrog.Room"); if the label was never learned, map it with `!activeroom <tab label>=<room>`. (Alias: `!switchroom`.)

entries.title: !roomshell
entries.summary: Dumps the room window's child controls (class, id, visibility) to the bot log — the diagnostic used to find the tab buttons in the first place.
entries.details: Dumps the room window's child controls (class, id, visibility) to the bot log — the diagnostic used to find the tab buttons in the first place. Only needed when tab switching stops working after a Camfrog update.

entries.title: !role <user> <owner|admin|staff|trusted|none> · !roles
entries.summary: Roles: owner > admin > staff > trusted > everyone.
entries.details: **Roles:** owner > admin > staff > trusted > everyone. Owners and admins run every admin command. **Staff** get admin powers only on the commands granted to staff (costumes, personas, conversation starters, DJ bans, mod fines, casino bans, cam pause, OBS scenes by default). Admins can hand out staff/trusted; only owners can make admins. `!roles` lists everyone. Also in the admin panel under **Roles & Permissions**.

Also editable in the admin panel under **Bot Admins**. Use the Camfrog login username, not a display name. (Alias: `!botadmins`.)

entries.title: !activeroom <tab label>=<room>

entries.details: **Maps a Camfrog tab to a room.** The room id from the network ("PepeFrog.Room") and the label Camfrog prints on the tab ("Pepe's Pad") are unrelated strings, so Pepe has to be told which is which — e.g. `!activeroom Pepe's Pad=PepeFrog.Room`. He learns most of these on his own once he's seen a room's window, but a room he's never had open won't be switchable until it's mapped. entries.title: !model
entries.summary: Tiered AI model control with per-function overrides.
entries.details:
Tiered AI model control with per-function overrides.


**Tiers:** **primary** (ask/roast/chatty) | **secondary** (charts/polls/prompts) | **background** (memory/trivia/summaries)

**Functions:** ask, roast, chatty, chart, imagine, poll, trivia, memory, summary


**Presets:**

`!model preset quality` — Opus / Sonnet / Haiku

`!model preset max` — Opus / Opus / Opus

`!model preset balanced` — Sonnet / Haiku / Haiku

`!model preset budget` — Sonnet / Haiku / Local

`!model preset local` — everything local Ollama

`!model preset off` — disable all AI (tools still work)


**Tier control:**

`!model all [model]` — set all tiers

`!model primary opus` — set a specific tier


**Per-function override:**

`!model ask opus` — override just !ask to use Opus

`!model chatty local` — override chatty to use local

`!model roast sonnet` — override roasts to use Sonnet

`!model ask reset` — remove override, fall back to tier

`!model reset overrides` — clear all overrides


**Info:**

`!model status` — show tiers + active overrides

`!model list` — list models, presets, and functions


**Intelligent Router:**

`!model preset intelligent` — dynamic model selection based on complexity, budget, and user feedback

`!model mode smart` — LLM-classified routing (uses local gemma3:4b to classify complexity, ~2s). Routes: simple→Haiku, moderate→Sonnet, complex→Opus

`!model mode fast` — rule-based routing (instant, no LLM). Routes: simple→Haiku, moderate→Haiku, complex→Sonnet

The router adapts over time — if users react negatively to a cheaper model's responses, it auto-upgrades. If a model consistently gets positive feedback, it may downgrade to save cost.


**Budget Control:**

`!model budget [amount]` — set daily budget (e.g. `!model budget 5` for $5/day)

`!model budget` — show current spend + remaining

`!model costs` — detailed cost breakdown by model and function

`!model feedback` — show quality scores per model based on user reactions


Models: opus, sonnet, haiku, local, intelligent, off. Auto-falls back to local when API credits run out. Persists between restarts.

entries.title: !reserve fund <pool> <amount> <reason>
entries.summary: A Fed grant: move PAT from the Federal Reserve into a protocol pool (not repayable, never a wallet). The same as !econ fund.
entries.details: Under economy v2/v3 (layers on) this is the **Fed grant**, the same as `!econ fund <pool> <amount> <reason>`: it moves PAT the Federal Reserve already holds into one of the protocol's pools - `house`, `bank`, `mm`, `fortknox`, `casino`, `incentives`, `lotto` or a pad vault `room:<room id>` - with a written reason. It is not repayable and nothing is minted; never into a wallet. A dry run first, then `!econ fund confirm <id>` within 2 minutes. A grant that would take the Fed below its floor is flagged and needs the confirm twice (the next daily tick mints the Fed back up, inside the monthly caps). Fort Knox, the Casino vault and pad vaults take at most what fits under their cap. A grant into the House, Bank or Market maker is protocol capital (the protocol takes shares at today's price, so stakers' share price doesn't jump). It's tagged “reserve fund”: never counted as House profit. For a repayable top-up use `!econ fedloan`. With the layers off it is the old v1 top-up of the Casino vault, Lotto pot or House.
examples: !reserve fund casino 2m refill the casino vault for the weekend

entries.title: !reserve pay [user] [amount]
entries.summary: Pay a player out of the Federal Reserve (the bank heist's vault).
entries.details: Pay a player out of the **Federal Reserve** (the bank heist's vault). It moves PAT that's already in the vault — nothing is created — and it can't pay out more than the Reserve holds. Amounts take `k`/`m` (`50k`, `1.5m`). **Off under economy v2/v3** (layers on): the Fed never pays a wallet - it fills pools only (`!econ fund` / `!econ fedloan`).

entries.title: !turf end
entries.summary: Ends the turf war season immediately — normally it runs 30 days and settles itself.
entries.details: **Ends the turf war season immediately** — normally it runs 30 days and settles itself. Crowns the highest Turf Score, pays the prize (everything the streets banked into the season pot, matched from the incentive budget; with no winner the pot rolls over), sends all business banks to the Federal Reserve and convoy cargo to Fort Knox, and **refunds every stake** to whoever held the borough (a disbanded gang's to its members). It waits for a running claim, raid or convoy job to finish first. Ownership, banks, forts, upgrades and Turf Score all reset; gang rep is permanent and carries over. Announced in every room. `!turf season` (anyone) shows the standings, the day and the pot without ending anything.

entries.title: !turf reset

entries.details: Wipes turf ownership back to a blank map and refunds each held borough's stake to its owner's treasury. Gangs, members and treasuries survive. Lighter than `!gangs reset` — this clears the board, not the players.

entries.title: !gangs reset
entries.summary: The start-over button.
entries.details: The start-over button. Dissolves **every** gang — members, treasuries, **rep**, Turf Score — and clears the whole map including banks and stakes. Nothing is refunded and there is no undo, so it asks first: `!gangs reset confirm` to go through with it. Distinct from a season ending, which keeps rep and hands stakes back.

entries.title: !vault mint [amount] [reason] · !reserve mint [amount] [reason]
entries.summary: The admin mint: prints PAT into the Federal Reserve only, with a written reason (dry run + confirm).
entries.details:
**The admin mint - into the Federal Reserve only.** `!vault mint <amount> <reason>`, `!reserve mint <amount> <reason>` and `!econ mint <amount> <reason>` are the same written-policy mint (policy "admin"): a dry run first, then `!econ mint confirm <id>` within 2 minutes, journaled in the mint log, announced in every room. It has no monthly cap of its own but counts toward `mintcap_total` (unlimited by default). It never lands in another pool or a wallet: naming a pool (`!vault mint casino 500k ...`) is refused - mint into the Fed, then move it with `!econ fund <pool> <amount> <reason>` (a grant) or `!econ fedloan <pool> <amount> <reason>` (a loan). Amounts take `k` and `m` suffixes.

`!reserve auto on|off` / `!reserve floor <amount>` are the v1 auto-top-up (off, and refused while the economy layers are on). Plain `!reserve` is public and shows the balance.
examples: !vault mint 5m restock the Fed after the event
!reserve mint 5m restock the Fed after the event

entries.title: Economy tuning — admin panel
entries.summary: Every rake, tap and split in the game is editable in the Sink Rates card without touching code: the arena/fight and hold'em rake rates, the tip tap, the treasury-withdrawal laundering…
entries.details: Every rake, tap and split in the game is editable in the **Sink Rates** card without touching code: the arena/fight and hold'em rake rates, the tip tap, the treasury-withdrawal laundering cut, the **sink cap** (the single biggest lever on how much PAT reaches the heist vaults), bank payout and cap multipliers, the mint rate, the season-pot share, and how much incoming vault PAT goes to the Reserve (the rest goes to the casino jackpot). **PAT Routing** decides where the PAT goes for everything Pepe charges — commands, music, voices, heist gear, blackjack losses, rake, lotto, bingo, wager and market fees, fines, loan interest: up to three destinations per row (the casino jackpot, the Reserve, Fort Knox, the vault of the room the PAT was spent in - turf businesses stopped taking a share on 2026-10-11 - or - for room-specific spending like commands, song requests, voices and shout-outs - the **room's owner**, 10% by default, paid weekly from the Reserve; a room with no owner leaves it in the Reserve) as a % of the price, and whatever isn't routed goes to the Federal Reserve — spending never burns PAT. **Economy v3 (live):** casino play and the wager fee go to the House, market and pool fees to the Market maker, loan interest to the Bank, fines and the bounty / shop fees to the Reserve, and spending in a room 50% Fort Knox / 50% the pad's vault. The same table says which pool **pays** each reward — level-ups (25k every level + a milestone of 250k × level/5 every 5th level), the welcome PAT, connect bonuses, redeem codes, chat raffles, top mic of the hour, `!beg`, Pictionary, turf income and the season prize: under v3 they all come out of the **incentive budget** (each within its weekly allowance; the Fed tops the budget up every Monday), never straight from the Federal Reserve. Turf upkeep, upgrades and claim/invasion buy-ins go to the Reserve. The **Vault flows & shortfall** table (under Automint) shows every PAT in and out of each vault by day and source, the daily shortfall, and a suggested automint. Prices and rewards that used to be hardcoded — heist buy-ins, showdown, turf claim/invasion, lotto ticket, bingo card, wager/market/loan fees, `!beg`/mic/Pictionary rewards — are rows in the Sink Rates card. **Automint** tops up a vault on a schedule (a daily amount, minted hourly) while it's below a target you set — the gap the economy can't fill on its own. **Shop Items** prices everything buyable plus the bonuses items carry (Bottle Service XP, burner heat reduction), and **Voice Store** handles per-voice pricing and royalties.

entries.title: !likeness [kind off|on]
entries.summary: Opt out of being snapped, clipped, looked at or roasted - and earn a cut when people do it.
entries.details:
It's a public chatroom, so everyone starts **opted in**. When a paid command uses you, you get a **likeness royalty** - a cut of the price, paid to your PATV wallet by the website after a **24 h hold**: mic clips and chat quotes 40%, `!snap` / `!clip` 40%, being a cam reference in `!imagine` / `!video` 40% (split), `!look` / `!camroast` 15%, `!roast` 10%. The cut comes out of the platform's share, never the pad owner's.

`!likeness <kind> off` refuses that kind of command on you **before anything is charged** (and you earn nothing for it). Kinds: `clips` (mic clips + chat quotes), `snaps` (`!snap` + `!clip`), `cam` (`!look`, `!camroast`, cam references), `roast`, `soundboard` (your mic clips on soundboards), `all`. `!likeness` alone shows yours. The same switches, your earnings and what's held are on the website at [/settings/likeness](/settings/likeness).

Nobody can use a likeness command on someone who blocked them, at most 3 per person per room every 10 minutes, and one per person per 5 minutes from the same payer. Cloning your voice is opt-in only (`!clonemyvoice`).

entries.title: !sb [clip]
entries.summary: Make Pepe play a soundboard clip on the mic - a few PAT per play, free for clips you own.
entries.details:
`!sb` lists what you can play in this room: the room's own board (Prime Time pads), the **global** board, this season's board and the **packs**. `!sb <clip>` plays one (the closest label wins). Per play: common **1,000**, rare **2,500**, epic **5,000** PAT, the season board 2,500 (unlimited with a Season Pass), a room clip whatever its owner set - and **free** for packs you own. Legendary clips are own-only.

Everyone shares the limits, owners and Season Pass included: one sound per person every 45 s (6 per 10 min), the same clip once per room every 3 minutes, one sound per room every 12 s, at most 3 waiting. Season Pass clips jump the soundboard queue. A clip that can't start within a minute is refunded.

Pad owners and room mods: `!sb on|off` switches it in the room (`!say` isn't affected), `!sb add <label> = <line> -v <voice> -p <price>` adds a line Pepe says, `!sb addmic <label> @user` adds that person's last mic-up (unless they typed `!likeness soundboard off` - they earn 30% of every paid play), `!sb remove <label>`. Clips in a community (cloned) voice pay its owner 30%.

Buy packs, the season board, All-Access and legendaries - and preview every clip - at [/soundboards](/soundboards), or tap 🔊 Soundboard on a pad's Live tab.
examples: !sb add Welcome = Welcome to the pond! -p 500

entries.title: !clonemyvoice
entries.summary: Clone your own voice so Pepe can speak in it - opt-in, you set the prices, delete it any time.
entries.details:
`!clonemyvoice` sends you a private link to the consent page: plain-language terms, an 18+ confirmation and your consent. You then get a one-time **phrase** and a short **script** to read on the mic - alone, in ONE turn, at least 30 seconds. Pepe checks that it's you (the phrase, its code and the script, nobody else on the mic) and the voice goes live: automatically for accounts 30+ days old at level 5+, otherwise after a quick staff review.

Your voice starts **unlisted**. On [/voices/mine](/voices/mine) you decide whether it's in the store, its prices (per use up to 10,000; an unlock 100,000-1,000,000), your cut (10-50%, 30% by default), whether others may make it say anything (off unless you turn it on) and whether pad owners may use it on soundboards. Your cut is held 24 h and paid daily.

`!clonemyvoice delete` (then `!clonemyvoice delete confirm`) deletes it: it stops at once, it's removed from both voice servers, and anyone who unlocked it gets half their PAT back. Only your own voice - never someone else's, a celebrity or an impression - and adults only.
